title: Client-side resequencing and preserve toolcall atomicity over SSE
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a client-side resequencing strategy and handoff semantics so that streamed outputs delivered over SSE preserve atomic tool/function-call boundaries and structured output integrity even during reconnects, reorders, or partial replays. This ticket covers protocol framing tweaks, client buffering behavior, backpressure interactions, and compatibility shims for older clients that expect simple newline-delimited JSON events.
background: We see intermittent out-of-order arrival and duplicate fragments under proxy-induced connection churn. Toolcall frames must be delivered to downstream consumers exactly once and in order for correctness; current naive pass-through leads to partial function-call deliveries and duplicate tool invocation in some integrations. Prior work (ENG-314159, ENG-27183) touched framing and resume tokens but did not provide a client-side invariant guaranteeing atomic toolcall delivery in the face of resequencing.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Spike complete: implemented a prototype in the web SDK that buffers up to 2MB or 250 events and reorders by incoming sequence-id. Observed tail-latency increase of ~9ms for typical 8-12 token chunks - acceptable for P1 trade-off.

2026-02-20 - Design review: PM Sasha Li and Designer M. Ortega recommended clear UX fallback (show partial content vs block). Agreed to prefer correctness for function calls (block until boundary satisfied) and provide progressive text for non-toolcall outputs.
2026-03-02 - Security/Privacy note from Security: ensure resume tokens are opaque and not logged. We added token redaction to client debug logs. (See attachment PR)
2026-03-10 - QA: Added e2e test harness that simulates delayed fragment reordering and duplicate replay. Found a bug where tombstone markers were not propagated to SDKs; hotfix drafted in PR #4921.
2026-03-12 - Engineering: Beginning rollout to canary clients (10% of hosted API traffic) behind feature flag. Monitoring parser error rate and toolcall duplicate count.
decisions: Adopt per-fragment monotonic sequence IDs assigned at server egress (sequence_id + stream_epoch) to allow stable reordering across reconnects.
Introduce explicit boundary markers for function/toolcall start and end rather than relying on JSON tokenization; this reduces ambiguity for structured outputs.

Client will implement a holdback buffer with a conservative watermark policy: hold fragments until contiguous sequence range is available or until a configured timeout elapses, then emit partials for non-toolcall content but never emit incomplete toolcall frames.
Backward compatibility: if client detects legacy framing (no boundary markers), fall back to legacy behavior but surface a compatibility warning in telemetry.
Do not change server-side timeout semantics for active streams; client-side buffering handles transient reorders instead of requiring server changes to SLOs.
